question: Find the equation of the plane that passes through the point $(2, 1, -1)$ and perpendicular to the line of intersection of the planes $x + 2y - z = 5$ and $3x - y + 4z = 7$.
explanation:
Normals to the given planes are $\vec{n}_1=(1,2,-1)$ and $\vec{n}_2=(3,-1,4)$.

Direction of the line of intersection is given by $\vec{n}_1 \times \vec{n}_2$.

Compute cross product:

$\vec{n}_1 \times \vec{n}_2 = (7,-7,-7)$.

This acts as the normal to the required plane.

Using point-normal form with point $(2,1,-1)$:

$7(x-2)-7(y-1)-7(z+1)=0$.

Simplifying gives $7x-7y-7z=14$.
